To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the direct synthesis of H 2 O 2 can be achieved by using bimetallic Pd based NC catalysts supported on TiO2.

(i) the direct synthesis of H 2O2 from the oxidation of H 2 by O 2 over Pd catalysts is strongly promoted by doping the Pd NCs with Ga and In, and to a lesser extent with Sn and Ni; and (ii) Pd NCs are more active and stable than Pd nanoparticles for the direct H 2O 2 synthesis.
PdSn and Ga NCs supported on TiO2 are highly efficient catalysts for the direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of highly active and selective Pd based bimetallic catalysts for the direct H2O2 synthesis from H2 andO2.
the development and characterization of bimetallic Pd-based catalysts with high performance for the direct synthesis of H 2O2 from hydrogen and oxygen.
the synthesis of PdSn and Ni Ga In bimetallic NCs supported on TiO2 and their application as catalysts for the direct synthesis of H O2 from H2O2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dopants studied in this thesis are effective in enhancing the activity of Pd catalysts for the direct synthesis of H 2O2, but the effect of dopants on selectivity is more complicated.

the presence of dopant metal(s) in a bimetallic Pd based nanocrystal catalysts is beneficial for the direct synthesis of H O2, and that the type and amount of the dopant(s) can be tuned to maximize the overall H O2 productivity.

the presence of a metal dopant in a colloidal Pd catalyst can enhance the overall H2 O2 productivity and/or the H2O2 yield, but the extent of the promotional effect depends on the type of the dopant metal and its amount.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of dopants to Pd catalysts is beneficial to the H2O2 synthesis reaction and the dopants can be classified as promoters or inhibitors.
the direct synthesis of H 2 O 2 from H 2 and O 2 can be achieved in the presence of Pd based bimetallic catalysts with the addition of a halogen or an acid.
the addition of dopants can enhance the H2O2 yield and/or H2O2/SO4 2 selectivity for Pd catalysts in both acid and base free and acid catalyzed conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the direct synthesis of H202 is possible without the need for acid or halide promotors.
the direct H2O2 synthesis can be efficiently promoted by the incorporation of metal dopants in the Pd NCs.
the direct synthesis of H 2O2 can be achieved without the addition of halide and/or acidic promotors, by using Pd based bimetallic NC catalysts.
